Apple TV came away with the most wins of any network at last night's Emmys, beating out the likes of HBO. Here's what HBO boss Casey Bloys had to say about Apple's victory.

HBO chief praised Apple TV but admitted competing against a trillion-dollar company is 'a little scary'

Apple TV has long been compared to HBO, with both prioritizing quality over quantity. Apple has sometimes even been called "the new HBO."

The Emmys last night further validated that notion, with Apple TV beating out HBO, Netflix, and others to become the most-awarded platform of the night.

Apple TV earned a total of 29 trophies, making it the "most-awarded network of the year," with standout performances from shows like Widow's Bay. HBO came in second with 21 wins.

Following the Emmys ceremony, HBO boss Casey Bloys was asked by Deadline about Apple's performance. Here's what he said:

DEADLINE: How do you feel about Apple TV's performance? They were the number one platform for the first time at the Emmys. What do you think? BLOYS: Well, I'm happy, because I think they're a phenomenal competitor, Zack and Jamie. Look, we've always had great competitors going back—Showtime, FX, AMC, Netflix, Amazon—so Apple, everybody keeps us on our toes, and I think that's when we do our best work. They're a trillion-dollar company, and that's a little scary, but we're going to keep doing what we've always done, which is make the best shows.

Bloys has been with HBO since 2004 and became head of programming in 2016. His track record speaks for itself, and his response to Apple's win was largely gracious and congratulatory.

However, the most interesting part of his comment was the line: "They're a trillion-dollar company, and that's a little scary."

We don't know the specifics of Apple TV's internal budget, but there's no question that Apple's overall financial firepower is far greater than most of its competitors—including HBO.

Coincidentally, Paramount is currently trying to acquire HBO (along with the rest of Warner Bros. Discovery) in a bid to better compete with tech giants like Apple and Amazon.

Does size automatically confer an advantage? Perhaps. But many networks have proven that money is only a small part of what it takes to produce content audiences love.

Apple TV costs $14.99 per month, or you can get it at a discount through the Apple One bundle.
